nodes.summary: In every execution, if the event at position $a$ happened before the event at position $b$, then the Lamport timestamp of $a$ is smaller than the Lamport timestamp of $b$ (Lamport 1978).
nodes.title: The clock condition

nodes.summary: The state is a counter $c(p) \in \mathbb{N}$ for each process $p$ together with the timestamps assigned so far. An event $e$ of process $p$ gets the timestamp $t = \max(c(p), s) + 1$, where $s$ is the timestamp already assigned at the position that $e$ receives from; $s = 0$ if $e$ is not a receipt or if no timestamp has been assigned at that position. The step sets $c(p)$ to $t$ and appends $t$ to the timestamps.
nodes.title: One step of the Lamport clock algorithm

nodes.summary: An event of an execution, for a type $P$ of processes, consists of the process in $P$ it belongs to and, if it is a receipt, a natural number: the position in the execution of the event whose message it receives. The structure does not require that position to be earlier than the event itself.
nodes.title: Event

nodes.summary: If position $a$ happened before position $b$ in an execution, then the execution has an event at position $a$ and an event at position $b$.
nodes.title: Happened-before relates positions of the execution

nodes.summary: Lamport's happened-before relation on the positions of an execution is the transitive closure of one step of happened-before: $a$ happened before $b$ when there is a chain $a = i_0, i_1, \dots, i_k = b$ with $k \ge 1$ in which each $i_m$ precedes $i_{m+1}$ by one step.
nodes.title: Happened-before

nodes.summary: If position $a$ happened before position $b$ in an execution, then $a < b$.
nodes.title: Happened-before goes forward in the execution

nodes.summary: The clock algorithm over an execution applies one step of the algorithm to each event in order, starting from all process counters $0$ and no timestamps. The result is the final counters together with the timestamps assigned to the events, in order.
nodes.title: Running the Lamport clock algorithm

nodes.summary: If position $i$ precedes position $j$ by one step of happened-before in an execution, then the Lamport timestamp of $i$ is smaller than the Lamport timestamp of $j$.
nodes.title: One step of happened-before raises the timestamp

nodes.summary: In an execution, position $i$ precedes position $j$ by one step when $i < j$, both positions hold events, and either the two events belong to the same process or the event at $j$ receives the message of the event at $i$.
nodes.title: One step of happened-before

nodes.summary: After the Lamport clock algorithm has run over an execution, the counter of each process is at least the timestamp of every event of that process in the execution.
nodes.title: Process counters dominate their timestamps

nodes.summary: Let $e_0, \dots, e_{n-1}$ be an execution and let $t_k$ be the Lamport timestamp of $e_k$. If $i < j < n$ and $e_i$ and $e_j$ belong to the same process, then $t_i < t_j$.
nodes.title: Lamport timestamps increase along each process

nodes.summary: Let $e_0, \dots, e_{n-1}$ be a well-formed execution and let $t_k$ be the Lamport timestamp of $e_k$. If $j < n$ and $e_j$ receives the message sent by the event at position $i$, then $t_i < t_j$.
nodes.title: A receipt is stamped later than its send

nodes.summary: Let $e_0, \dots, e_{n-1}$ be an execution, and extend it by appending further events. For every $i < n$, the Lamport timestamp of the event at position $i$ is the same in the extended execution as in the original one.
nodes.title: Appending events does not change earlier timestamps

nodes.summary: Let $e_0, \dots, e_{n-1}$ be an execution and let $i < k \le n$. The Lamport timestamp of $e_i$ in the whole execution equals its Lamport timestamp in the prefix $e_0, \dots, e_{k-1}$.
nodes.title: A timestamp depends only on a prefix containing its event

nodes.summary: The Lamport timestamps $t_0, \dots, t_{n-1}$ of an execution $e_0, \dots, e_{n-1}$ are computed by Lamport's clock algorithm. Every process keeps a counter, initially $0$. For $k = 0, \dots, n-1$ in turn, let $c$ be the current counter of the process of $e_k$, and let $m = t_i$ if $e_k$ receives the message sent by the event at position $i$ with $i < k$, and $m = 0$ otherwise. Then $t_k = \max(c, m) + 1$, and the…
nodes.title: Lamport timestamps

nodes.summary: In every execution, if the event at position $a$ happened before the event at position $b$, then position $a$ precedes position $b$ in Lamport's total order.
nodes.title: Lamport's total order extends happened-before

nodes.summary: In every execution, for any two distinct positions $a \ne b$ that both hold events, $a$ precedes $b$ or $b$ precedes $a$ in Lamport's total order.
nodes.title: Lamport's order is total

nodes.summary: Fix a linear order on the processes. In an execution $e_0, \dots, e_{n-1}$ with Lamport timestamps $t_0, \dots, t_{n-1}$, position $a$ precedes position $b$ when $a < n$, $b < n$, and either $t_a < t_b$, or $t_a = t_b$ and the process of $e_a$ is smaller than the process of $e_b$.
nodes.title: Lamport's total order

nodes.summary: An execution $e_0, \dots, e_{n-1}$ is well formed when every receipt names an earlier event: whenever $e_j$ receives the message sent by the event at position $i$, then $i < j$.
nodes.title: Well-formed executions

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
